memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message: 'A people that has come out of Egypt covers the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I will be able to fight them and drive them away.'" But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not put a curse on those people, because they are blessed." - Num 22:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam lays out Balak's request to God, and the Lord's reply could not be clearer. Three things are stated plainly: do not go with them, do not curse them, and here is the reason: they are blessed. God leaves no room for confusion.

What a striking declaration about Israel. Despite all their failures in the wilderness, despite their grumbling and rebellion, God calls them "blessed." Their standing did not rest on their performance but on His covenant promise. He had set His love upon them, and nothing would change that.

This is the wonder of grace. God does not bless His people because they have earned it, but because He has chosen to be faithful. Israel could not undo the blessing by their sin, and no enemy could undo it by their curses. It rested entirely on the character of God.

The same grace secures those who belong to Christ. In Him, believers are blessed with every spiritual blessing, not because we are worthy but because God is gracious (Eph 1:3). When God declares you blessed in Christ, no accusation, no failure, and no enemy can overturn His word. Rest in the sure declaration of your Father.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rest your standing before God on your performance or on His grace?
2. How does it comfort you that God calls His people "blessed" despite their failures?
3. What accusation or fear do you need to surrender to God's word of blessing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious Father, thank You that my blessing in Christ rests on Your faithfulness, not my performance. When I fail, remind me that Your declaration over me stands sure. Amen.
